Shabbat Parshat Devarim
(Tisha B'Av,

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "Eichah yashvah badad" and the Tzemach Tzedek's interpretation that it refers to a lofty level of Divine isolation, questioning how this relates to the plain meaning of lamentation.

translations.translation: "How she sits alone, the city that was full of people..." And it is explained
by the Rebbe, the Tzemach Tzedek
(whose name is Tzemach)
that "she sits alone" is as it is written,
"God alone will lead him,"
"Surely, alone, the eye of Yaakov."
And this is accomplished through "full of people," etc., as will be explained later.
And it must be understood: "Eichah" is an expression of wonder and astonishment,
and according to the interpretation that "she sits alone" means that Israel will ascend to the level of "God alone will lead him,"
the level of "alone"
(outside the camp – as a superiority)
above the chain of descent,
what is the wonder and astonishment in this?
Also, it is necessary to understand the connection of this interpretation with the simple interpretation,
for the simple interpretation of "Eichah she sits alone" is the greatness of the descent, etc.,
therefore they read Eichah on Tisha B'Av, when the destruction occurred,
and what is the connection of the simple interpretation with the Tzemach Tzedek's interpretation that "she sits alone" is a superiority.
And this will be understood by first prefacing the greatness of the elevation
(according to the Tzemach Tzedek's interpretation of the verse)
in "she sits alone,"
which is the matter of "surely, alone, the eye of Yaakov."
For the precision of "surely, alone, the eye of Yaakov"
(specifically Yaakov)
is as our sages said,
"Not like Avraham, about whom it is written 'mountain,' etc., and not like Yitzchak, about whom it is written 'field,' etc., but like Yaakov, who called it 'house.'"
And this means that the elevation of "surely, alone, the eye of Yaakov" that will be in the future,
and particularly in the Third Holy Temple,
is the matter of "like Yaakov, who called it 'house,'"
that the inheritance of Yaakov is an inheritance without borders,
the level of Ratzon d'Ratzin (Will of Wills),
as our sages said,
"Whoever delights in the Sabbath is given an inheritance without borders... the inheritance of Yaakov..."
And this elevation that will be in the future comes through the precedence of the "she sits alone" of the exile, etc.
And this is the matter of what our sages likened
the matter of exile to the judgment of Adam HaRishon with expulsion
[For just as Adam HaRishon is the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He,
so too are Israel
(who were judged with expulsion)
"the plant of His planting, the work of His hands" of the Holy One, blessed be He,
literally a part of God from above],
And just as Adam HaRishon was judged with expulsion for the sake of the elevation that would come afterward,
until the elevation of the Giving of the Torah, which is even higher than the elevation of "and He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it" of Adam HaRishon
(as will be explained later),

And this is like at the Giving of the Torah, there were seven generations that removed the Shechinah from below to above, and then seven generations that drew down the Shechinah from above to below until the Giving of the Torah,
Similarly, also after the Giving of the Torah, they needed to come to the Land of Israel
and build the Holy Temple,
"the place that God will choose,"
which is higher even than the Tabernacle, about which it is written, "and I will walk in a tent,"
there were then several vicissitudes, etc., until the Holy Temple was built,
and afterward there was the destruction of the First Temple, and they came to the elevation of the Second Temple,
which is higher than the First Temple, as it is written,
"The glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former," which refers to the Second Temple, which was greater than the First Temple in building and in years,
And similarly, regarding the destruction of the Second Temple,
they will afterward reach the elevation of the Third Temple, which will be built very soon by our righteous Mashiach,
which is higher than the First Temple and also than the Second Temple,
and as our sages said
(cited above)
"Not like Avraham, about whom it is written 'mountain,' and not like Yitzchak, about whom it is written 'field,' but like Yaakov, who called it 'house.'"
And this is also the continuation in the verse, "she has become like a widow," but not a widow, God forbid,
for since the intention of the descent is for the sake of the ascent that will come afterward,
it is not a true descent,
and therefore "she has become like a widow" with the letter "kaf" of comparison.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ultimate purpose of creation is for God to have a dwelling place in the lower worlds, achieved through service, progressing from Adam to the Giving of the Torah to the Temples, culminating in the future.

translations.translation: And the concept is,
as explained by the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
that the ultimate intention of creation is that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place for Himself in the lower worlds,
that this intention is fulfilled through the service of the souls of Israel,
as per the statement, "In whom did He consult?"
(regarding all of creation)
"In the souls of the righteous."
And behold, at the beginning of creation, "the world was created in its fullness,"
"the main dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower worlds,"
meaning that the "main dwelling of the Shechinah" is the level of the Surrounding Light.
For "Shechinah" is the level of the Filling Light,
"Shechinah" from the term "dwelling" and "being clothed,"
but the "main dwelling of the Shechinah" is the level of the Surrounding Light, and even to the Surrounding Light that is above worlds,
as explained at length in the continuation of the Maamarei HaHilula.
And although the drawing down of the Surrounding Light is accomplished specifically through the service of Adam HaRishon and the souls of Israel, as above,
nevertheless, immediately at the beginning of creation, "the world was created in its fullness,"
meaning
(not that there was an actual drawing down of the "main dwelling of the Shechinah,"
for this is accomplished specifically through service,
but rather)
that it was created in a way that it would be prepared and fit for the revelation of the light of the "main dwelling of the Shechinah,"
and the actual drawing down is specifically through service.
And this is the matter of "and He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it,"
that through the service of Adam HaRishon, an addition of light was made in the Garden of Eden.
For the Garden of Eden in itself is the level of the Filling Light
(and that "the world was created in its fullness" means only that there was a place prepared for the revelation of the Surrounding Light,
as above),
but within the level of the Filling Light itself, there is an advantage in the Garden of Eden over the entirety of the world in two matters:

first, that the light that is clothed in the worlds is from the level of the seven lower Sefiros, while in the Garden of Eden, the three upper Sefiros shine; and second, that in the worlds there is only knowledge of existence, while in the Garden of Eden there is revelation of essence.
But all this is only the level of the Pervading Light.
"And He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it,"
that through this he would draw down the level of the Surrounding Light,
the level of the "main dwelling of the Shechinah."
However,
even the level of "to work it" that was in the Garden of Eden is not comparable to the service after the Giving of the Torah,
and as our sages said
regarding the mitzvos of the Patriarchs,
that they were only "like a fragrance."
And even though they said this regarding the Patriarchs,
since until the Giving of the Torah there was the decree that "the upper ones shall not descend below and the lower ones shall not ascend above," etc.,
this was also the case regarding Adam HaRishon.
And even though he was commanded
(and therefore he had the advantage of "one who is commanded and does")

— at any rate, regarding the six commandments — the commandment as it is below before the Giving of the Torah is not like the commandment after the Giving of the Torah, since the upper ones had not yet descended below.
And also according to what is explained in the maamar there, that the service of Adam HaRishon was more elevated than the service of the Patriarchs,
for Adam HaRishon was the handiwork of the Holy One, blessed be He, and was in the Garden of Eden,
etc., nevertheless,
(as explained in the maamar there)
it is not comparable to the level of "Your name is like poured oil,"
the essential drawing down of the Giving of the Torah.
However,
even the service after the Giving of the Torah is not comparable to the revelation that was in the Holy Temple
(and particularly through the "to work it and to guard it" in the Holy Temple),
"the place that God will choose,"
for then specifically a dwelling place was made for Him, blessed be He,
a permanent dwelling.
And within the Holy Temple itself, the matter of a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, was greater in the Second Temple,
for even though in the Second Temple five things were lacking,
nevertheless, "the glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former" in building
(place)
and in years
(time)
— the definition of lower things — from the perspective of the world itself.
However, the main dwelling place will be specifically in the future,
through the Torah and mitzvos that will be observed then,
for then the observance of the mitzvos will be in ultimate perfection,
as per the statement,
"And there we will perform before You as the commandments of Your will,"
specifically there,
and as explained at length by the Rebbe Maharash.
